items.title: Naqvi did not object to India’s refusal to collect Women’s Asia Cup trophy, claims BCCI official
items.description:
Asian Cricket Council (ACC) Chairman Mohsin Naqvi had no objection to the Indian women’s team refusing to collect the Asia Cup trophy from him, said Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) Vice President Rajeev Shukla on Monday.
The remarks came as criticism mounted over Shukla and BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia’s interaction with Naqvi during Sunday’s final in Dubai.

items.title: China imposes travel curbs to protect 'national security'
items.description:
China imposed sweeping travel restrictions on its citizens on Tuesday, including exit bans on those deemed to endanger the country’s “industrial or technological security”.
Citizens who violate technology import and export regulations could be banned from leaving China, the State Council said.
Those who engage in illegal activities abroad could be “prohibited from leaving the country for a period of six months to three years from the date of their return to China”.

items.title: Constitution must remain supreme, every exercise of public authority must be within its limits: FCC CJ
items.description:
Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan on Tuesday stressed constitutional supremacy and observed that every public exercise must be in accordance with it.
“The Constitution must remain supreme, and every exercise of the public authority must remain within its constitutional boundaries,” he said while addressing an event in Islamabad.
The FCC chief justice noted that the Constitution was the “supreme expression of the collective will of the people”.
He went on to say that every institution created under it derived its authority from it and remained subject to its limits

items.title: War on Iran resulted in munitions shortfall for US, confirms Pentagon report
items.description:
WASHINGTON: The United States has acknowledged that its war on Iran resulted in “strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply” for America.
The admission came in the first Pentagon Inspector General’s report on the US-Israeli war on Iran. The report, released on Monday, provides a detailed account of the campaign’s cost, damage and impact on American weapons stocks, confirming some of the concerns that news organisations had reported for months.

items.title: These Baloch fishermen don’t want fast food
items.description:
The people living along Balochistan’s beaches have always fought to defend the sea that feeds them. For years, fishermen from Gwadar to Lasbela accused large trawlers from Sindh of sweeping up everything in their path when they entered Balochistan’s twelve-nautical-mile waters. Their prohibited wire nets or “gujja” trapped juvenile fish, breeding stock and species with scant commercial value, leaving little behind. This fight defined the Haq Do Tehreek movement that united thousands around a single demand: save the sea before it is emptied.

items.title: How India's transnational repression cases expose unequal accountability across borders
items.description:

Fifteen years before a guilty plea in New York exposed an Indian government employee’s alleged role in a plot to assassinate a Sikh activist, the body of a 15-year-old Bangladeshi girl hung from the India-Bangladesh border fence for hours.

items.title: To heal a divided family
items.description: CENTURIES before Charles Darwin theorised our shared human evolution from the fish, multiple traditions linked humanity to a single common fold. The 18th BRICS summit in Delhi saw Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as the host leaning on the Sanskrit phrase ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’ — the world is a family — to underpin the spirit of unity, which unfortunately eludes much of mankind. The ancient aphorism is a good but an overstretched reminder of seeing everybody as an equal human being. items.title: Rethinking relief
items.description:
THE prime minister’s decision to subsidise petrol purchases for motorcycle and small-car owners is understandable amid consumer outcry against high fuel rates. But it is unlikely to offer much relief.
The Rs75bn package may sound substantial but is barely a fraction of annual petrol sales. Its reach will be narrower because eligibility depends on conditions such as vehicle and SIM ownership. A monthly subsidy of Rs2,000 for motorcycles and Rs3,000 for small cars may help households, but cannot shield them from sustained global oil price increases. items.title: New US rules change how international students can stay in America
items.description:
WASHINGTON: A major change in the US immigration system is set to take effect on Tuesday, requiring international students to keep closer track of how long they are authorised to remain in the country.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is ending the longstanding “duration of status” system for F-1 students and replacing it with a fixed period of admission.
